title: Production of AAV Virus by Iodixanol Gradient Ultracentrifugation
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
materials: Production of AAV Virus by Iodixanol Gradient Ultracentrifugation
DMEM with high glucose, L-glutamine and sodium pyruvate (Thermo Fisher Scientific 11995-065 or equivalent).
Opti-MEM I Reduced Serum Medium, GlutaMAX (Thermo Fisher Scientific 51985-034 or equivalent).
TrypLE Select (Thermo Fisher Scientific 12563-011 or equivalent)
OptiPrep™ Density Gradient Medium (60% (w/v) solution of Iodixanol in water (sterile)) (Sigma D1556-250ML or equivalent)
Phenol Red solution, 0.5%, liquid, sterile-filtered (Sigma P0290 or equivalent)
Glycerol for molecular biology, ≥99.0% (Sigma G5516 or equivalent)
Eppendorf Easypet 3 electronic pipette controller (or equivalent)
Gilson P1000, P20, P200, P10 single channel pipettes
Disposable cell scraper (Fisher Scientific 08-100-242 or equivalent)
Culture dish, 150 mm (VWR SC25383-103 or equivalent)
Fluorescence inverted microscope (Carl Zeiss, Olympus, or equivalent)
Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Units, 100 KDa (Sigma UFC910024 or equivalent)

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary media and solutions for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic by adding 50 mL of FBS and 5 mL of Antibiotic-Antimycotic to 500 mL of DMEM; store at 4ºC.
Prepare DMEM with 4% FBS and 1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic.
Prepare PEI solution: Dissolve 1 mg of PEI (Polysciences 23966) in 1 mL of PBS, adjust pH to between 4 and 5 using 12N HCl, and sterilize via a 0.22 µm filter unit.
Prepare 10X Gradient Buffer (GB) (100 mL) and filter sterilize using a 0.22 µm vacuum filter system.
Prepare Iodixanol gradient solutions: 15% (100 mL), 25% (70 mL), 40% (150 mL), and 60% (150 mL). Mix well and store at 4ºC.
Prepare washing buffer.

steps.title: Seed 293 Cells
steps.instruction: Seed cells to achieve target confluency for transfection.

substeps.instruction: Seed 2 × 10^7 293 cells in 15 cm dishes (split confluent plates 1:2) to achieve ~70% to 80% confluency by the next morning.
Maintain cells in complete DMEM/10% FBS/1% anti-anti, using 20 mL of culture medium per plate.
Split cells before reaching confluency by trypsinizing with TrypLE.
Combine 5 mL of OptiMEM in a 15 mL polystyrene tube and vortex briefly for 5 seconds.
Add 1.1 mL of PEI to the mixture, vortex briefly for 5 seconds, and incubate for 5-10 min at room temperature.
Add 0.61 mL of the resulting mixture dropwise to the medium in each dish and swirl to disperse evenly.

steps.title: Post-Transfection Cell Culture
steps.instruction: Maintain cells and incubate until harvest.

substeps.instruction: Change the medium to 20 mL of DMEM/4% FBS/1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic 24 hours post-transfection.
Incubate cells until 72 hours post-transfection.

steps.title: Harvest and Lyse Cells
steps.instruction: Collect cells and perform freeze-thaw cycles to release AAV.

substeps.instruction: At 72 hours post-transfection, scrape each plate with a cell scraper and transfer the mixture to a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 500 x g for 15 min at 4ºC to collect cell pellets.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 10 mL of 1X gradient buffer; mix by pipetting.
Freeze the 50 mL tube in dry ice in an ice bucket, then thaw in a 37ºC water bath. Repeat the freeze/thaw cycle 3 more times.
After the final thaw, add 50 U/mL Benzonase (2.6 µL of enzyme per 10 mL) to the suspension.
Incubate at 37ºC for 30 min.
Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 3,000 x g for 15 min at 4ºC and collect the supernatant.

steps.title: Build Iodixanol Gradient
steps.instruction: Layer Iodixanol solutions in a Beckman Polycarbonate Bottle.

substeps.instruction: Add the 15% solution (3 mL) to the bottom of the tube using serological pipets.
Using a 10 mL syringe with a Hamilton metal hub needle, slowly inject subsequent layers from the bottom up: 25% (3.5 mL), 40% (3 mL), and 60% (3 mL).
Ensure the needle is placed just above the bottom of the tube during injection.

steps.title: Ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Purify AAV using the iodixanol gradient.

substeps.instruction: Slowly drip the Benzonase-treated supernatant onto the top layer of the gradient.
Divide the supernatant (typically 10 mL for 10 plates) into 2 tubes if necessary, balancing them with gradient buffer.
Weight the tubes to ensure the difference is less than 0.05 g.
Close the tubes and centrifuge at 58,000 rpm in a Beckman Type 70Ti rotor for 90 min at 18ºC.

steps.title: AAV Recovery and Concentration
steps.instruction: Extract the AAV-rich fraction and concentrate using centrifugal filters.

substeps.instruction: Prime an Amicon Ultra-15 Centrifugal filter unit by adding 5 mL wash buffer and spinning at 3,000 g.
Using a 10 mL syringe with a Hamilton metal hub needle, extract ~4 mL of solution from 1-2 mm below the interface between the 40% and 60% gradient buffer layers.
Transfer the collected solution to the primed Amicon Ultra-15 unit, add washing buffer, and centrifuge at 3,000 rpm at 4ºC.
Continue washing and centrifuging until the final volume is reduced to 150 µL.

steps.title: Storage
steps.instruction: Aliquot and store the purified virus.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot viral samples and store at -80ºC for long-term storage.
